definitions.explanation: A solid substance in which atoms or molecules are arranged in a regular, repeating pattern. Also the process of forming such a structure.
The tangible result or culmination of sustained effort, love, or dedication. A figurative extension of the crystallization metaphor.

examples.japanese: {雪|ゆき}の{結晶|けっしょう}は{美|うつく}しい。
{塩|しお}が{水|みず}から{結晶|けっしょう}した。
{顕微鏡|けんびきょう}で{結晶|けっしょう}の{構造|こうぞう}を{観察|かんさつ}した。
examples.english: I observed the crystal structure under a microscope.

examples.notes: A common expression referring to a child born of a loving relationship.

examples.japanese: この{作品|さくひん}は{長年|ながねん}の{努力|どりょく}の{結晶|けっしょう}だ。
examples.english: This work is the fruit of many years of effort.

examples.japanese: チーム{全員|ぜんいん}の{汗|あせ}と{涙|なみだ}の{結晶|けっしょう}がこの{優勝|ゆうしょう}だ。
examples.english: This championship is the product of the entire team's sweat and tears.

notes:
USAGE:
Also functions as a suru verb: {結晶|けっしょう}する (to crystallize). The figurative sense 2 is very common in everyday Japanese, especially the phrase {愛|あい}の{結晶|けっしょう} (fruit of love, i.e., a child).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {雪|ゆき}の{結晶|けっしょう}: snow crystal
- {結晶|けっしょう}{構造|こうぞう}: crystal structure
- {愛|あい}の{結晶|けっしょう}: fruit of love (a child)
- {努力|どりょく}の{結晶|けっしょう}: fruit of one's efforts
